added: Each type of dance (contra, English country dance, square) now has its own dialects and its own active dialect. Choose the type at the top of Settings › Dialect, and every dance reads in the dialect of its own type.
The new-dance Type setting can be Last used, so a new dance starts as the type of the last new dance you saved.
changed: Dialects no longer accept gendered role words such as "gents" or "ladies" in role names, move wording, or a dialect's name. A dialect saved earlier with one shows the built-in role name instead and is renamed if its name used one.

added: `DialectsByForm` holds the dialect each dance form is shown in; `forDance` picks a dance's.
`genderedRoleWords`, `genderedRoleWordIn` and `shownDialectName` find and mask the gendered role words a dialect may not show.

Classify `custom_dialects_ecd`, `custom_dialects_square`, `active_dialect_ref_ecd`, `active_dialect_ref_square` and `last_used_dance_form` as shareable preferences; the two custom-dialect keys sync as whole collections.
changed: `Dialect.validate` reports `gendered_role_term` for a gendered word in a role term, substitution, move wording or branch entry, and `Dialect.fromJson` replaces a gendered role term with the Larks/Robins term and drops gendered substitutions and wordings.
`syncCollectionEntries` labels a dialect whose name is gendered with `Dialect.customName`.

`FigureRenderer.moveWordingTemplate` seeds an English Country Dance movement's wording with each switch group (`[{?flag}words]`) written as the condition `[if flag then words]`, so the seed saves and reads as the movement does by default.
